impact: Strong consumer spending and tariff refunds support the soft-landing case, but resilient demand also backs the hawkish Fed lean that pressures growth holdings like NBIS, PLTR and BE; little direct effect on his positions.
summary: Target's fiscal Q3 comparable sales rose 5.6% vs about 3.8% expected, driven by 5% higher traffic, with digital comps up 9.8%; net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1B and adjusted EPS was $2.65 vs $2.07 expected. The quarter included $301M of pretax tariff refund benefits, about $0.50 per share. Target raised full-year EPS guidance to $10.65 to $11.40 from $9.90 to $10.90 and sees sales growth around 6%, though shares dipped premarket.
title: Target comps jump 5.6%, raises guidance; tariff refund adds ~50 cents EPS
